subject: Re: Follow-up & DPA clarifications — Acme Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa.green@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + DPA clarifications (next steps)

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really valuable to hear more about Acme Payments' fraud-detection pipeline and how you expect models to be used in production. Quick recap and the follow-ups we discussed: 

- Recap: intent is real-time scoring for transactions (sub-200ms), logs stored for 30 days for model feedback, and certain PII elements (card token, user id, device id) will be sent.
- Ask from you: confirm controller/processor relationship language in the DPA, subprocessors list, and our breach notification SLA.
- Next steps from our side: I’ll circulate a short note addressing controller/processor roles and data residency options, and attach our standard DPA for reference. Ben will also pull our current subprocessors list and SOC2 summary.

I’ve attached the standard DPA. Can you upload the redline your legal team prepared (if any)? If easier, I can jump on a 20-min call with your DPO to walk through the key items.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachment: Redwood-DPA-standard-20270420.docx
From: Alyssa Green <alyssa.green@acme-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Payments DPO <privacy@acme-payments.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up + DPA clarifications (next steps)

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the DPA. I attached a redline from our legal team (20270421-Acme-DPA-redline.docx). Top-line questions we flagged:

1) Controller vs. processor: We need the contract to reflect that Acme Payments is the controller for transaction data and Redwood is the processor. We saw some mixed language in Section 2 that could be interpreted as co-controller.
2) Subprocessors: please provide an up-to-date subprocessors list + a commitment to notify us prior to onboarding any new subprocessors handling production PII.
3) Breach notice: request 48-hour initial notification for incidents affecting production PII (we currently have 72 hours in your standard DPA).
4) Data residency: we need a US-only residency option for production logs for at-rest storage.

Can Ben or someone provide SOC2 Type II evidence and the current subprocessors list? Also confirm whether Redwood accepts a limited liability cap carve-out for data breaches (we listed proposed language in the attached redline).

Alyssa Green
Head of Product Security
Acme Payments
alyssa.green@acme-payments.com
Attachment: 20270421-Acme-DPA-redline.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa.green@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + DPA clarifications (next steps)

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks for the detailed redline — very helpful. Quick responses to each of the four asks below, and next steps.

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed — Redwood is comfortable and will accept explicit processor language. We’ll update Section 2 to remove any co-controller wording and add an explicit "Redwood acts solely as a processor" clause.

2) Subprocessors: Ben is attaching the current subprocessors list (we maintain a published list). We commit to notifying customers 30 days prior to adding new subprocessors that could process production PII; if you need a longer notice window we can discuss.

3) Breach notice SLA: We can commit to an initial notification within 48 hours for confirmed incidents impacting production PII and will include a follow-up with remediation details within the next 7 calendar days.

4) Data residency: We offer a US-only data residency option for at-rest logs for Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted customers we can restrict storage to US regions and apply controls, but if you require contractual data residency guarantees for Hosted we recommend Dedicated (we can include language in the DPA to reflect the option and the required configuration).

Other items: Regarding your proposed liability carve-out, I forwarded the redline to our legal team for review — we typically handle liability caps in the main agreement, but we can escalate if your language is standard for regulated payments vendors.

Attached: subprocessors_list_20270422.pdf (Ben) and SOC2-TypeII-summary.pdf.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll send an updated DPA with the processor language and breach SLA updated by Friday.
- Ben to share the subprocessors list and SOC2 slides (in this thread).
- If useful, let’s schedule a 30-min call between your DPO and our legal/security (I’m available next Tue/Thu).

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: subprocessors_list_20270422.pdf
Attachment: SOC2-TypeII-summary.pdf
From: Alyssa Green <alyssa.green@acme-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Payments DPO <privacy@acme-payments.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up + DPA clarifications (next steps)

Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turn. Received the subprocessors list and SOC2 summary from Ben — looks good at first pass. A couple of follow-ups before we route to legal: 

- Can you confirm the subprocessors list includes the inference engine hosting provider and any third-party logging/monitoring vendors? We flagged those specifically.
- For the 48-hour breach notice, can you add a sentence that confirms the initial notice will include known scope (systems affected, PII categories) and whether exports/backups were impacted? That will help our incident triage.

If you can send the updated DPA with those two clarifications, I’ll aim to get legal's final sign-off next week. If not, we can set the DPA review for a short call — DPO is available Wed morning.

Thanks,
Alyssa
